newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich vows to be sworn in again.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich vows to be sworn in again.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich predicted Monday that he would be re-elected despite breaking House rules, apparently ruling out suggestions he step aside.
"Tomorrow, when I'm sworn in I'll be the first Republican speaker to be sworn in twice in a row in 68 years," he told a Cobb County Chamber of Commerce meeting.
Gingrich said he could not talk about his problems with a House ethics investigation into his financial dealings and spoke mainly about his political philosophy.
On Dec. 21, Gingrich admitted he had broken House rules and brought discredit to the chamber.
On Tuesday, the House is to vote on his re-election as speaker.

Rep. Michael Forbes of New York is the only Republican member of Congress to publicly state that he will vote against Gingrich, but others have said he should stand aside until the ethics questions have been resolved.
